xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfNonComplianceOfBoardC:
During the quarter ended September 30, 2024, and up to December 29, 2024, the composition of the Board of Directors of the Company was not in compliance with Regulation 17(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as half of the Board members were not Independent Directors.
This deviation arose due to regulatory requirements applicable to the Company under Rule 55(8) of the Arms Rules, 2016. As the Company holds arms manufacturing licenses issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), any change in directorship, including the appointment of Independent Directors, necessitates prior approval from these Licensing Authorities.
Accordingly, the Company submitted an application for approval of the appointment of two Independent Directors to the Licensing Authorities on September 3, 2024. The MHA granted its approval on November 12, 2024 and DPIIT's approval was received on December 30, 2024, following which the Board appointed Mr. Ravi Kapoor and Ms. Rashmi Joshi as Independent Directors on the same day.
The Company was thus unable to comply with the stipulated Board composition requirements solely due to the time taken for regulatory approvals, which were beyond the Company's control. Upon receipt of the necessary approvals, the Company promptly regularized its Board composition in compliance with Regulation 17(1).

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs:
Company has challenged revision of Annual Rateable Value (“ARV”) & property tax bill based on revised ARV for set of Triennial period 2004-05 to 2023-24 (extended till the date) raised by PCB which was contrary to the settlement between the Company and PCB. The decision on Appeal filed before the Pune District Court and Writ Petition filed before Bombay High Court is pending. However, the Company has paid the entire amount demanded under protest. This litigation will not have any adverse financial impact on the Company.
Property Tax from 2004-05 till FY 2019-2020 has been paid in full under protest - in event of Company succeeding in appeals - favourable impact to the tune of INR 30.50 crores.
Property Tax from FY 2020-21 to 2023- 24 – in the event of Company (i) succeeding in appeal - Company would save property tax to the extent of INR 17.83 crores. (ii) not succeeding in appeal - there would be financial impact to the tune of INR 17.83 crores.
Hon’ble Bombay High Court has, vide order dated September 06, 2024 (“the Order”), disposed of the writ petition with instructions to avail of the alternate remedy under the Cantonments Act, 2006 by filing an appeal before the Pune District Court (“Appellate Authority”) and depositing the balance disputed amount under protest. The Appellate Authority has been instructed to dispose of the appeal on or before October 11, 2025
